evidence.title: Russia And ASEAN Strengthen Strategic Ties As Lavrov And Kao Discuss Security, Trade And Global Cooperation
evidence.body: [e001:f01] RUSSIA: Russia and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation, with officials discussing regional security, economic ties and ways to expand collaboration. [e001:f02] Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov met ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn in Moscow on Tuesday, where both sides highlighted their long-standing relationship and shared interest in international cooperation. [e001:f03] Lavrov described the partnership with ASEAN as a continuing priority for Moscow, saying Russia viewed the bloc as a reliable partner after years of working together on international issues. [e001:f04] He also said both sides shared an interest in shaping what he described as a fairer, multipolar world order across Greater Eurasia and neighbouring regions. [e001:f05] Russia Highlights ASEAN’s Regional Role During the meeting, Lavrov said Russia had consistently respected the ASEAN-centred security architecture in Southeast Asia. [e001:f06] ASEAN brings together 11 member states, including Singapore, and plays a central role in regional forums focused on political, economic and security cooperation. [e001:f07] Lavrov also pointed to possible new areas of collaboration between Russia and ASEAN. [e001:f08] These include maritime security, pandemic preparedness, youth engagement and customs-related matters. [e001:f09] The discussions come as regional governments continue to engage with major international partners on security, trade and cross-border challenges. [e001:f10] For Southeast Asia, maritime security remains an important area of cooperation because regional economies depend heavily on shipping routes and international trade. [e001:f11] ASEAN Calls For Dialogue And Stability Kao highlighted existing cooperation between Russia and ASEAN across several sectors, including energy, education, tourism, culture, technology and efforts to combat international crime. [e001:f12] Representing a region of nearly 700 million people, Kao said ASEAN’s population had a strong interest in a peaceful and stable international environment. [e001:f13] Kao said dialogue could help reduce tensions and support peace, underscoring ASEAN’s continued emphasis on engagement between countries. [e001:f14] Cooperation Amid Global Uncertainty The meeting highlighted the two sides’ stated intention to maintain close ties and explore additional areas of cooperation. [e001:f15] However, the remarks reported from the Moscow meeting focused on broad priorities rather than specific policy changes, funding commitments or new agreements. [e001:f16] Both Lavrov and Kao presented dialogue and multilateral cooperation as important parts of their approach to international relations, while signalling interest in expanding cooperation across a range of sectors.

evidence.title: Mexico Moves Toward Airline Mega-Merger With Limited Restrictions
evidence.body: [e003:f01] The country’s antitrust regulator is moving toward authorizing the transaction with relatively limited operational restrictions, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing six people familiar with the discussions. [e003:f02] The merger would establish Grupo Más Vuelos, a holding company overseeing two airlines that together account for approximately 75% of Mexico’s domestic flights. [e003:f03] The anticipated approval would represent a significant shift in Mexico’s airline market, concentrating much of the country’s domestic air travel under one corporate group while testing regulators’ ability to safeguard competition and affordable fares. [e003:f04] Three people familiar with the regulatory discussions told Reuters that the airline group would also be required to continue operating under a low-cost business model. [e003:f05] The agreement has not received final approval, and regulators are still determining how some of the proposed conditions would be implemented and monitored. [e003:f06] Market Concentration Raises Competition Concerns The proposed merger would bring together Mexico’s two leading low-cost carriers, which have steadily expanded their domestic presence and overtaken traditional rival Aeromexico in market share. [e003:f07] The competitive implications are particularly significant on routes where passengers already have limited alternatives. [e003:f08] Despite those concerns, regulators are not expected to impose major restrictions on the number of flights the companies can operate at Mexico’s busiest airports, according to people cited by Reuters. [e003:f09] The airline is concerned that regulatory conditions may prove insufficient to constrain the combined group’s market power. [e003:f10] Financial Pressures Drive Consolidation The transaction, announced in December 2025, follows several difficult years for Mexico’s aviation industry. [e003:f11] The merger is structured as a combination of equals, with both carriers expected to retain their separate brands and operating identities. [e003:f12] Volaris Chief Executive Officer Enrique Beltranena played an important role in advancing the agreement, Reuters reported, citing a person familiar with the airline’s operations. [e003:f13] Add as Preferred Source Government Airport Strategy Adds Political Dimension The proposed merger also carries implications for Mexico’s efforts to increase traffic at government-operated airports. [e003:f14] According to Reuters, two people familiar with the matter described government pressure to advance the transaction, partly because Volaris and Viva Aerobus are leading operators at Felipe Ángeles International Airport, outside Mexico City. [e003:f15] Approval Would Test Mexico’s New Antitrust Regulator The merger represents an early high-profile challenge for the CNA, which replaced Mexico’s previous competition authority in 2025. [e003:f16] In 2007, authorities prevented Mexicana from acquiring Aeromexico, Reuters noted.

evidence.title: Swiss Franc strengthens as US Dollar slips on dovish Fed signals
evidence.body: [e004:f01] USD/CHF depreciates as US Dollar pulls back after New York Fed President John Williams signals no rate hikes for await crucial September CPI reports to gauge upcoming Federal Reserve policy receives support as Swiss 10-year government bond yield rebounds to near 0.56%.USD/CHF extends its losses for the second consecutive day, trading around 0.8320 during Asian hours on Wednesday. [e004:f02] The currency pair depreciated as the US Dollar (USD) lost ground following dovish remarks from New York Federal Reserve President John on Tuesday, Williams noted that while he maintains his view that one more rate hike may be appropriate this year, he does not foresee additional rate increases in 2027. [e004:f03] In response, the CME FedWatch Tool suggests markets are currently pricing in roughly a 77% probability that the Fed will leave interest rates unchanged this month, alongside an 88% chance of a rate hike in focus now shifts to the US September CPI inflation data scheduled for release later in the North American session, which could offer clearer direction on the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy path. [e004:f04] CPI is expected to show a year-over-year rise of 3.6% in September, up from 3.4% in August. [e004:f05] Meanwhile, Core CPI—which excludes volatile items—is projected to tick up to 2.5% year-over-year from 2.4% in the previous on the Swiss 10-year government bond rose to near 0.56%, tracking a broader decline in global bond yields and falling oil prices. [e004:f06] This drop in oil came after Russia agreed to release diesel supplies onto global markets, easing concerns over fuel shortages and reducing the immediate need for fiscal household support. [e004:f07] Higher bond yields could provide support for the Swiss Franc (CHF).Meanwhile, Swiss inflation rose to a two-year high of 1% in September, driven mainly by elevated energy prices amid the prolonged Middle East conflict, though it remained well within the Swiss National Bank’s 0–2% target range. [e004:f08] The Swiss National Bank (SNB) kept its policy rate at 0% in September, with Vice Chairman Martin noting that no rate adjustment is currently needed due to low and stable inflation and limited spillover risks, adding that the Swiss economy was working "very well." While most economists expect the policy rate to remain unchanged through 2027, markets continue to price in a rate hike by year-end and roughly three hikes by the end of seen consolidating as UOB tightens near-term rangeStrategists at UOB Group note that their early-October call for USD/CHF to have “likely entered a range-trading phase between 0.8245 and 0.8365” remains broadly intact, even after the Dollar “rose to a high of 0.8350” yesterday. [e004:f09] Between 2011 and 2015, the Swiss Franc was pegged to the Euro (EUR). [e004:f10] The peg was abruptly removed, resulting in a more than 20% increase in the Franc’s value, causing a turmoil in markets. [e004:f11] The Swiss Franc (CHF) is considered a safe-haven asset, or a currency that investors tend to buy in times of market stress. [e004:f12] The Swiss National Bank (SNB) meets four times a year – once every quarter, less than other major central banks – to decide on monetary policy. [e004:f13] The bank aims for an annual inflation rate of less than 2%. [e004:f14] Higher interest rates are generally positive for the Swiss Franc (CHF) as they lead to higher yields, making the country a more attractive place for investors. [e004:f15] Macroeconomic data releases in Switzerland are key to assessing the state of the economy and can impact the Swiss Franc’s (CHF) valuation. [e004:f16] The broader European Union is Switzerland’s main economic partner and a key political ally, so macroeconomic and monetary policy stability in the Eurozone is essential for Switzerland and, thus, for the Swiss Franc (CHF).

evidence.title: Aussie Holds Firm on China Inflation, Fed Signals
evidence.body: [e005:f01] Key Moments AUD/USD trades around 0.6990 in Asian hours, extending gains into a second consecutive session. [e005:f02] China's September CPI rises 0.9% YoY while PPI jumps to 5.0%, both closely watched by AUD traders. [e005:f03] Markets await US September CPI, with headline inflation expected at 3.6% YoY and core at 2.5% YoY. [e005:f04] The Australian Dollar is maintaining its recent strength against the US Dollar after the release of fresh inflation data from China, a key destination for Australian exports. [e005:f05] Chinese Inflation Data: Mixed CPI, Stronger PPI China's National Bureau of Statistics reported that the country's Consumer Price Index increased 0.9% year-over-year in September, edging up from 0.8% in August but falling slightly short of the 1.0% market consensus. [e005:f06] On a month-over-month basis, Chinese CPI rose 0.2% in September, down from a 0.4% gain previously and below expectations for a 0.3% rise. [e005:f07] The Producer Price Index advanced 5.0% year-over-year in September, accelerating from a 3.8% increase in August and beating forecasts for a 4.5% gain. [e005:f08] Chinese Inflation Indicators - September Actual Consensus Previous CPI YoY 0.9% 1% 0.8% CPI MoM 0.2% 0.3% 0.4% PPI YoY 5.0% 4.5% 3.8% US Dollar Eases After Fed Commentary The US Dollar has softened, lending additional support to AUD/USD, following comments from New York Federal Reserve President John Williams. [e005:f09] Speaking on Tuesday, Williams reiterated that he still views one more rate increase as potentially appropriate this year, but he does not anticipate further rate hikes in 2027. [e005:f10] According to the CME FedWatch tool, Fed funds futures traders are still largely positioned for at least one additional US rate increase in 2027. [e005:f11] Attention Turns to US September CPI Release Market participants are now focused on the upcoming US Consumer Price Index data for September, due later in the North American session. [e005:f12] The release is viewed as a key input for assessing the Federal Reserve's next policy steps. [e005:f13] Consensus forecasts point to headline US CPI rising 3.6% year-over-year in September, up from 3.4% in August. [e005:f14] Core CPI, which excludes more volatile components, is projected to climb 2.5% year-over-year, compared with 2.4% previously. [e005:f15] US CPI Expectations - September Expected Previous Headline CPI YoY 3.6% 3.4% Core CPI YoY 2.5% 2.4% IMF Meetings: Potential Catalyst for Volatility Strategists at Scotiabank highlight the upcoming IMF meetings as a potential source of renewed market turbulence, stating they "will provide a significant amount of headline risk as market participants assess policymakers’ appetite for continued tightening in an environment of elevated oil prices and broadening inflationary pressures." evidence.title: ICYMI - Three Fed officials signal inflation fight continues; Williams sees no 2027 hike
evidence.body: [e006:f01] With October largely priced out, Tuesday’s trio keeps December in focus for the next move. [e006:f02] Williams’ comments on 2027 cap how far markets can push expectations for the peak rate. [e006:f03] That should limit the upside for longer-dated Treasury yields and the dollar unless the data turns. [e006:f04] Barkin’s warning that shocks are continuing gives the hawkish camp an opening if inflation stays sticky. [e006:f05] Oil is the swing factor. [e006:f06] Williams’ benign outlook assumes energy won’t add to inflation next year, so a renewed crude surge, for example from escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites, would undercut that view and strengthen the case for more tightening. [e006:f07] For now, oil is effectively a direct input into Fed pricing.
